kitDescription: Ein is an Electric sniper who fights largely through summoned 'Near Feathers'. She enters every battle with 4 feathers already summoned, and each feather that gets summoned immediately strikes an enemy for true damage (damage that ignores defence). Her Burst III summons 6 more feathers at once, and for the next 10 seconds raises her own true damage and her charged-shot damage, while simultaneously hitting the highest-defence enemy for a large true-damage nuke. Separately, whenever the team's burst chain reaches Stage 3 — whether she casts it or another Burst III unit does — she gains a 10-second attack buff. Her sniper fire also feeds itself: every full-charged shot leaves her charged damage boosted for the following shot, so in practice she is permanently charge-buffed while firing.

redAssertions: battle-start feather count === 4 separate damage events — driver folds the 4 into ONE flatDamage 363.24 (=4×90.81). Shape divergence, identical expected total; lumping is kit-silent and the S6 blind flagged split-vs-merge as a ⚑ itself.
feather 90.81-halving counterfactual is a no-op against the driver's 363.24 lump — same lumping root cause, not an independent failure.

S2 chargeDamagePct 80 carries durationShots === 1 (3 assertions: durationShots field, expiresFrame null, seconds-window counterfactual) — driver ships a permanent passive instead. Documented in the note; see gotcha 4.

6 feather hits per ein burst cast — driver ships a 34×90.81 = 3087.54 burstCast lump plus a 6×90.81 = 544.86 fullBurstEnd trickle (Prydwen COMMUNITY count, ⚑2). Count divergence 6 vs 34; this is the substantive RED.
(the 4 skipped S5 cases are the blind writer's own declared unobservables — summon indirection, target-selection collapse, feather noFb/noRange — not divergences)

Documented in the note, so DOCUMENTED_GAP — but the driver's infeasibility claim sits against game-mechanics §11's stated semantics, which is an engine-ordering question, not a kit question (gotcha 4).

Modeled correctly against its datamined source, but test E7 only asserts that zero-damage ticks exist and disappear when removed — it never asserts the SIDE EFFECT the block exists for (team gauge / full-burst count). 'Modeled ≠ working' is unproven here (gotcha 5).

gotchas.summary: Every ein rider — the 4-feather start lump, the 34-feather burst lump, the 6-feather trickle and the 300.02% nuke — is crit-eligible, which contradicts game-mechanics.md §9's explicit ruling that flavor:"true" flatDamage never crits; the driver's test PINS the higher-damage branch.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Deals 90.81% of final ATK as true damage' / 'Deals 300.02% of final ATK as true damage'. SSOT game-mechanics.md §9: 'TRUE DAMAGE NEVER CRITS (owner ruling 2026-07-21; engine `crit && !trueFlavor` guard), so `flavor:"true"` dots/flatDamage + `trueNormals` windows are crit-exempt.' damage-calculation.md §2c states the same ruling but names only dots (ada's grenade DoT). Driver's ein.test.ts E4/E5 assert `critEligible === true` on both the nuke and the feathers and PASS, and the test header argues the carve-out is 'DOT-scoped ... Prydwen-confirmed for Near Feathers' — a COMMUNITY claim placed above an owner ruling. Neither blind agent addressed it (S2b assumed riders 'crit at caster rate'; S6 set no crit field), so no blind corroboration either way. This is the one finding the blinds did not surface.
gotchas.suggestedFix: PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed — resolve the SSOT conflict before trusting the pin, do NOT adjust any number. Recipe: (a) grep the engine's `trueFlavor` guard in dealDamage and confirm whether it gates only the dot/tick path or all flavor:'true' instances, and whether the event's `critEligible` field is emitted pre- or post-guard; (b) `git log -S trueFlavor` + the 2026-07-21 DECISIONS entry to read the owner ruling's stated scope; (c) owner ruling on whether Near Feathers crit in game. If §9 stands as written, the engine must apply `crit && !trueFlavor` to flatDamage as well and the E4/E5 pins invert — that removes ~7–15% from the bulk of ein's output and touches every true-flavor unit (ada et al.). If the carve-out really is dot-only, amend §9 so the two SSOT docs stop contradicting each other. Leaving a contested behavior asserted by a green regression pin is exactly the 'passing tests don't justify known-wrong code' failure mode.

gotchas.summary: Feather instance counts are 34 per her burst plus 6 per full-burst end, against the prose's explicit '4 at battle start' + '6 summoned at burst' — roughly 185 feather hits per fight versus a kit-literal ~28 (~6.6×), on what is her largest damage term.
gotchas.evidence: Kit skill1: 'Summons 4 Near Feathers'; kit burst: 'Summons 6 Near Feathers'; kit skill2: 'Activates when Near Feather is summoned ... Deals 90.81% of final ATK as true damage' — one attack per summon, and no kit clause summons feathers at full-burst end. Driver ships 34×90.81 = 3087.54 (burstCast) + 6×90.81 = 544.86 (fullBurstEnd, fires on EVERY rotation including ones ein never bursts), sourced to Prydwen, flagged ⚑2 with recipe (U8 ein-focus recording) and tier 2. Both blinds independently derived the kit-literal 4 + 6/burst; S6 flagged the opposite risk ('if feathers persist and attack repeatedly, this model UNDERSTATES her'), so the direction is genuinely open. WHOLE-PICTURE: the driver's own model is internally inconsistent — 4 battle-start summons yield exactly 4 hits, but 6 burst summons yield 34. Either feathers repeat (then the t=0 four should repeat too) or they do not (then 34 is wrong). ein is already a listed kit-level board outlier (damage-calculation §6).
gotchas.suggestedFix: Keep as shipped and flagged (the ⚑ is properly formed), but tighten the documentation and resolve the inconsistency: state in the note whether the model's premise is 'feathers persist and re-attack' — and if so, why the 4 battle-start feathers do not. Then measure: an ein-focus recording (U8), counting true-damage popups per burst window and per inter-burst window, settles 34 / 6 / the battle-start 4 in one pass and is the same recording ⚑3 needs. Do not tune the count against the board.

gotchas.summary: Her own True Damage ▲55.3% burst buff never reaches the 3087.54 feather lump — the lump resolves at cast-instant in the skill2 slot, before the burst-slot buff registers — so the buff moves only ~0.7% of her total and the lump is under-credited ×1.553.
gotchas.evidence: Kit burst prose lists the self buffs BEFORE the 300.02% damage line; the buffs are same-cast self-grants. damage-calculation §5b (cinderella worked example) establishes that a caster's OWN cast-granted buff DOES apply to its own burst damage ('her own cast-granted HP→ATK conversion included'), while only ally full-burst-ENTRY auras are excluded by the boundary rule. Driver's own test E2 documents the ~0.7% drop as the measured consequence. S6 blind ordered its burst block buffs-first for exactly this reason and flagged the alternative as the thing to check.
gotchas.suggestedFix: This one is SSOT-derivable and should NOT be gated on measurement: move the feather lump so it resolves after the burst's self-buff block (author it in the burst slot below the buff block, or give it a ≥1-frame delaySec), citing damage-calculation §5b. CAUTION — land it together with gotcha 2, not before: the fix multiplies the largest term by 1.553 in the same direction that an over-stated 34 count already pushes, and a board ratio that currently looks acceptable may be riding compensating errors. Measure the cadence first, then land both, or land the ordering fix ENV-gated default-OFF.

gotchas.summary: A round-scoped window is encoded as a permanent passive on the grounds that durationShots:1 is mechanically infeasible on a shotFired trigger — but game-mechanics §11 documents durationShots as implemented with 'spent right after the shot so the Nth shot still benefits'.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Activates when attacking with Full Charge. Affects self. Charge Damage ▲ 80% for 1 shot(s).' game-mechanics.md §11 (IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-23): round-scoped windows end after the holder fires N bullets, and the count is spent right after the shot. Driver note claims the shotFired trigger applies the buff after the shot's damage is computed, yielding zero benefit (self-reported verification). Both blinds encoded durationShots:1; S2b called durationSec:1 the highest-leverage misread on this kit line.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Board impact is ~one shot in ~120 (an SR that always full-charges is continuously re-primed, so permanent ≈ literal from shot 2 onward) — no urgency. But if the driver's observation is right, that is an ENGINE ordering defect in the shotFired + durationShots interaction, not an ein problem: it would silently zero every future 'for N shot(s)' buff authored on a per-shot trigger. File it against the durationShots primitive with the two-line repro, rather than leaving the workaround as the precedent.

gotchas.summary: Test E7 proves the orb's zero-damage ticks exist, but never asserts the gauge side-effect that is the block's entire purpose — 'modeled ≠ working' is unverified for the orb.
gotchas.evidence: Override models the orb as a zero-damage permanent dot whose ticks feed skillGauge 560 per 2.83s (datamined special_burst_gauge 5.6 / 170f). E7 asserts orbTicks.length > 0, summed amount === 0, and that removing the dot removes the ticks. A zero-damage tick that failed to reach addGauge/skillGauge would pass all three assertions identically.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Add one discriminating assertion: removing the orb dot must reduce the comp's full-burst count (or the team's gauge-fill events) — per game-mechanics §6 a dot tick contributes the caster's flat target value, so at 560 per 2.83s over 180s the effect on rotation is large enough to be observable. Assert the rotation delta, not the ticks.

verdictRationale: All 8 kit lines are FAITHFUL or DOCUMENTED_GAP, so the rubric fraction is a literal 8/8 = 1.0 — but read that number narrowly: it scores kit-line encoding only, and three of the eight ride ⚑ gates while the highest-severity finding is scored outside the kit-line rubric. The blind re-derivations converged hard where it mattered most: both S2b and S6 independently chose stageEnter:3 for the ATK buff (the single highest-risk trigger read, where burstCast would halve uptime against helm as co-B3), both derived burstCast rather than fullBurstEnter for the burst self-lines, both collapsed the 10-target nuke clause to one instance, and both folded the on-summon payload into the summoning block. S5's six REDs are all shape or documented-gap divergences (lumping, durationShots, feather count), none a silent drop. Ranked findings: (1) crit-eligibility on true-flavored flatDamage contradicts game-mechanics.md §9's explicit owner-ruling text and is now PINNED by the driver's tests — PLAUSIBLE not confirmed, cross-cutting beyond ein, and it is the item neither blind surfaced; (2) the 34-feather cadence, properly ⚑-flagged but a 5.67× override of the prose's own '6' on her largest term, and internally inconsistent with the 4-summons-4-hits battle-start block; (3) the ⚑3 ordering gap, which — unlike the driver's framing — is answerable from damage-calculation §5b today and does not need the U8 recording, though it must land WITH the cadence measurement because the two errors point the same way and may currently be cancelling. GO is warranted because every kit line's encoding matches the prose, the two genuinely load-bearing trigger reads are triple-corroborated, and every divergence carries an estimate, recipe and tier; nothing here is a fudge. discriminationOk is FALSE for one reason: E1 asserts `applied.length >= ein's burst count`, which is equally green under the burstCast nearest-wrong — tighten to a strict `>` (helm fills B3 on ein's cooldown rotations) or assert an apply with no adjacent ein burstCast; also add the orb's gauge side-effect assert. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: the crit-on-true-damage ruling scope (§9 vs §2c) — I could not run the engine, and the driver's 'Prydwen-confirmed feathers crit' rests on a COMMUNITY claim sitting above a 2026-07-21 owner ruling; that single question moves the bulk of ein's output and every other true-flavor unit.
